result:
All 16 tasks are done, none failed and none were skipped, and every test suite passes on the final commit. Two tasks needed one fix round each; the other 14 passed review the first time. The work is on branch `d2/run-f2f843` as 19 commits, ending with one that records the final task statuses in the plan file. Nothing is pushed.

I ran every suite myself on the final code, with these results:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| plan-state | 252 passed, 0 failed |
| verify-tests | 58 passed, 0 failed |
| resolve-declared-paths | 91 passed, 0 failed |
| audit-stats | 8 passed, 0 failed |
| commit-safe (concurrent-commit, stale-lock) | PASS |

**What was built:**
- **`plan-state`:** check rule 16 validates the new `tests:` entries and test settings. `set … running` records `base_sha:`, which rule 17 validates. A new `plan-state tests <plan> <id>` command prints one task's named tests.
- **`verify-tests`:** a new helper that builds a "before" and an "after" copy of the repo, runs each named test in both, labels the result, prints the last lines of failing output, and cleans up on every exit path, including Ctrl-C and similar interrupts. Its test suite covers sh and dash.
- **Docs and prompts:** the executor, the implementer and reviewer prompts, the plan format, the planner, the updater, the S17 soft heuristic, the verifiability lens, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` all now describe named tests.

**The two fix rounds:**
- **task-format:** the doc didn't say which label wins when a test fits two of them. The spec's order was added.
- **task-tests-cmd:** one test couldn't fail, because it squeezed repeated spaces before comparing. It now compares the line exactly, and breaking the code makes it fail.

**Findings that may need a follow-up `/update`:**
- **Run time:** a real `verify-tests` run on the `plan-state` suite took 400 seconds. The executor text explains its 600-second limit with "about 85 s per run". 400 s is still under the 540 s threshold the task checks, but that wording may need updating.
- **Bash tool timeout:** when the Bash tool times out, no signal is sent. The command moves to the background and keeps running, so `verify-tests` isn't killed and cleans up on its own. The plan asked for this to be reported so the executor text can be updated.
- **Small reviewer suggestions, not acted on:**
  - a one-line guard so a `files:` path containing `..` or starting with `/` can't make `verify-tests` delete outside its temporary copy;
  - processes started by a test can outlive a signal sent to `verify-tests` alone;
  - a few tests could be clearer.

**Things to know:**
- **Gate-2 audit:** the plan's audit record still says "NOT READY — 4 blocking". The plan text already fixes all four findings, but no later audit round records READY.
- **Which plugin ran:** the run used the pinned plugin copy at `pde-pinned-c57de12`, so the new `verify-tests` step didn't check this run's own work, as the plan intended.
- **Untested awk versions:** only gawk is installed here, so the rule that the scripts also run under mawk and busybox awk was checked only by reading the code.
- **Leftovers outside the repo:**
  - the dispatch prompts in `C:\Users\Brett\d2-runs\pde-d2-run-f2f843-prompts\`, which you can delete;
  - some `/tmp/vt*` and `/tmp/final-*` log files;
  - two pairs of idle `python.exe` processes. They started at 12:18 AM (process IDs 33172 and 48596) and 3:37 AM (53376 and 38048), which looks like before this run, so I didn't touch them. The hung one an implementer left during the run is already gone.
